technical_and_design_decisions: Use Spring Security for authentication, HTTPS configuration, endpoint authorization, and role-based access checks.
Expose SSL/HTTPS and Basic authentication through documented application properties and configuration examples rather than implementing a separate security subsystem.
Represent security definitions and ACL rules as configurable policies mapping REST entities and operations to groups or roles.
Enforce ACLs in a shared authorization service so that the DSL Shell and Admin UI use the same policy decisions and default behavior.
Implement the Python processor as an isolated subprocess adapter using configurable Python executable and stdin/stdout communication with a documented record format.
Implement the R processor as an isolated Rscript subprocess adapter using stdin/stdout, avoiding a mandatory in-process native-library dependency.
Implement the Hive sink using HiveServer2 JDBC with configurable connection, table, batching, and serialization settings.
Upgrade Spring Core to version 4.1.1 and resolve resulting dependency, API, and compatibility issues across the increment.
Use automated unit, integration, security, processor, Hive, and regression tests as the primary verification approach.
Provide backward-compatible defaults where practical, with unrestricted read access and existing behavior retained when no ACL configuration is supplied.
assumptions: The increment is implemented in an existing Spring XD-style Java/Maven codebase with established module, shell, admin UI, and test infrastructure.
An existing authentication mechanism and user/group or role model are available for Spring Security integration; implementing identity providers, LDAP, OAuth, or user administration is out of scope.
The Admin UI has existing extension points for adding authorization checks and configuration screens.
The DSL Shell and REST APIs have identifiable command and endpoint authorization boundaries that can be mapped to policy names.
Python and R runtimes are external deployment prerequisites; runtime installation, licensing, and production operations are documented but not implemented.
The Python and R processors exchange one logical streaming record per line using a documented text or JSON representation and support configurable process lifecycle and error handling.
HiveServer2 is available for integration testing or can be represented by a test double; provisioning a Hadoop or Hive cluster is out of scope.
The Spring Core upgrade is limited to the specified 4.1.1 milestone and includes remediation of directly resulting compilation and regression issues.
Database schema or configuration persistence changes use the project's existing migration and persistence conventions.

Effort includes implementation, code review preparation, automated tests, documentation, and local integration verification by one developer; it excludes elapsed waiting time and separate reviewer effort.

activities.activity_description: Inspect the existing modules, build, security model, REST APIs, DSL Shell, Admin UI, processor abstractions, sink abstractions, configuration conventions, and test infrastructure. Produce the detailed implementation design and identify integration points and compatibility risks.

Implement or align configuration properties and startup wiring for HTTPS and Basic authentication on administration endpoints, including secure defaults, validation, failure behavior, configuration examples, and focused tests for U1.

Implement configurable entity- and operation-specific security definitions for REST APIs, including policy parsing, role/group matching, authorization integration, denied-access behavior, configuration validation, and unit/integration tests for U6.

Define ACL policy names and defaults for stream and related resource operations, integrate authorization checks into DSL Shell commands, handle unauthorized responses, and add configuration and security tests for U7.

Add Admin UI support for displaying and configuring relevant ACL settings, apply authorization checks to create, destroy, view, and related operations, handle denied actions consistently, and add UI/API tests for U8.

Evaluate native and subprocess integration against the streaming processor lifecycle, finalize the stdin/stdout adapter design, implement process startup and shutdown, record serialization, backpressure/error handling, configuration, documentation, and automated tests for U2.

Evaluate rJava, Renjin, and Rscript approaches against deployment and streaming constraints, implement the selected Rscript stdin/stdout processor adapter, provide configuration and lifecycle/error handling, document runtime prerequisites, and add automated tests for U3.

Implement a configurable Hive sink using HiveServer2 JDBC, including connection management, table/schema mapping, batching, retries and error handling appropriate to the existing sink model, configuration metadata, documentation, and integration tests for U4.

Update dependency management to Spring Core 4.1.1, compile and run the existing test suite, remediate API or behavior incompatibilities, review transitive dependency alignment, and verify SpEL and application-context behavior for U5.

Create end-to-end coverage across authentication, REST policies, Shell ACLs, Admin UI ACLs, external processors, Hive sink, configuration defaults, and the Spring upgrade. Fix integration defects and perform focused security and compatibility regression testing.

Document all new configuration properties, security definitions, ACL examples, HTTPS and Basic authentication setup, Python and R runtime requirements, processor data contracts, Hive sink setup, defaults, and troubleshooting guidance.

Update Maven modules, dependency and packaging metadata, sample configurations, automated build jobs, migration or upgrade notes, license notices where needed, and perform a clean build and release-candidate verification.
